newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hosken falls after results, says talks end.
newsitem.headline: Hosken falls after results, says talks end.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Hosken Consolidated Investments Ltd fell to a new year low on Friday after the firm reported a drop in year earnings and also withdrew an earlier cautionary notice, dealers said.
Shares tumbled to 395 cents in early trade, a drop of almost seven percent, but by about 0800 GMT were off their worst trading at 410 cents.
Some 91,900 shares worth around 375,000 rand had changed hands.

"(The results and the withdrawal of the cautionary) are probably the reasons whey they fell, for the simple reason that people speculating that whatever deals they were negotiating have probably fallen through," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.
Hosken, referring to earlier cautionary notices, advised shareholders on Friday that negotiations which it had been conducting had proved unsuccessful.

Its earnings per share before non-recurring items dropped to 11.0 cents from 19.6 cents in the previous 12 month period and share earnings after non-recurring items tumbled to 39.3 cents from 86.1 cents.

The fall follows the issue of a vast number of shares during the year in a rights offer to raise 186 million rand and attributable income for the year rose to 28.91 million rand from 18.24 million before.

The firm added that the results were not indicative of its expected performance in the year ahead as it now owned stakes in firms which should prosper through their active involvement in the cellular telephony, radio, mining and video sectors.
